diff_ref: evidence/g4-dc5/{score_arm.py, assert_dc1.py, make_arm.py, run_arm.sh} + MEASUREMENT.md (new, untracked measurement instrument + write-up under gate g4)

smells.finding: score_arm.py's score() (lines 149-218) does record-walking, per-call classification (shape/usage/state/other), and far-side detection all inline in one ~65-line function with several co-mutated counters (attempts, shape_errors, usage_reads, far_side, other_errors, state_refusals, carrying_calls). It is readable but each classification concern (shape vs usage vs far-side vs state) would be clearer as its own small function -- and the engine_invocations() undercount this review found (r7/r10, a hand-authored analysis instrument review) would likely have been caught sooner with the per-invocation counting logic isolated and unit-tested on its own.

score_arm.py and MEASUREMENT.md both carry long prose comments/docstrings explaining WHY a classification choice was made (e.g. why the server log is corroboration-only, why --help is not an error, why batching is counted as N invocations).

override.repo_standard: CREW_CONTEXT.md 'Verification Discipline' + global-everyone.md 'Pin a claim to the revision you read it at' -- this repo's convention is to make measurement/decision rationale explicit and durable in the artifact rather than leave it tacit, especially for a one-off instrument a second party must independently re-derive from.
override.reason: These are decision-rationale comments explaining a non-obvious methodological choice for an independent auditor, not comments compensating for unclear code that should have been refactored instead -- removing them would remove information this exact review needed to check the corrections (r10), so they earn their keep rather than deodorize a smell.
